subject: Decision Making
title: Prospect Theory Changes Economics
description: Learn Prospect Theory Changes Economics in one minute.

hook.text: Kahneman and Tversky proved that losing $100 hurts roughly twice as much as gaining $100 feels good.

buildup.text: Classical economics said gains and losses are symmetric. Prospect theory showed the emotional math is lopsided.

discovery.text: Loss aversion explains why people hold losing stocks, stay in bad jobs, and refuse fair gambles.

twist.text: The theory also showed that framing matters. A 90% survival rate feels better than a 10% death rate. Same fact.

climax.text: Prospect theory replaced rational choice as the model of real behavior. Humans are loss-averse, not utility-maximizing.

punchline.text: Losses hurt twice as much as gains feel good. That distortion drives decisions.

quiz.question: What is loss aversion?
options: Losses feeling roughly twice as painful as equivalent gains feel good
